statement.p: We consider another variation on this problem: now the boxes cannot be empty. Try to fill in the following table. You will be able to determine 3 out of 4 of the answers. We will talk about the last one as a group.

p.em: n distinct boxes, k balls, boxes CANNOT be empty

solution.p: The formula n! S(k,n) uses the number S(k,n) which is called the Stirling Number of the Second Kind. It turns out that we've asked a very hard problem!

We do have the tools at our disposal to give and understand the formula for S(k,n). However, the argument is a little more abstract than I usually like to cover in MATH 279. So you can just write down "n! S(k,n)" as the answer to this question (when it comes up) without knowing the particular formula for S(k,n).

Some more details: the number S(k,n) counts the number of ways to put n distinct balls into k identical boxes where boxes cannot be empty and repetition is allowed. Can you explain why we must multiply by n! in order to get the number of ways to use distinct boxes instead?

statement.p:
You want to give away 20 identical baseballs to 10 baseball fans. How many ways can this be done when \ldots
There are no restrictions on how you give them away.
The 20 identical baseballs are the balls. The 10 fans are the distict boxes. Repetition is allowed and boxes can be empty.
{20+10-1 \choose 20} = {29 \choose 20}
Every fan must get at least one baseball.
The 20 identical baseballs are the balls. The 10 fans are the distict boxes. Repetition is allowed and boxes cannot be empty.
{20-1 \choose 10-1} = {19 \choose 9}
Every fan must get exactly two baseballs.
There is 1 way to do this: everyone gets 2 baseballs.

You want to give away 20 distinct baseball caps (from different teams) to 10 fans. How many ways can this be done when \ldots
There are no restrictions on how you give them away.
The 20 distinct caps are the balls. The 10 fans are the distict boxes. Repetition is allowed and boxes can be empty.
10^{20}
Every fan must get at least one baseball cap.
The 20 distinct caps are the balls. The 10 fans are the distict boxes. Repetition is allowed and boxes cannot be empty.
10! S(20, 10)
Every fan must get exactly two baseball caps.
Every fan must get 2 caps. The number of ways to do this is
{20 \choose 2} { 18 \choose 2} {16 \choose 2} {14 \choose 2} {12 \choose 2} {10 \choose 2} {8 \choose 2} {6 \choose 2} {4 \choose 2} {2 \choose 2}
